title: AI Coding Market Scan
subtitle: 2026-03-28 · market
executive_summary: AI coding tools are moving from experimentation into repeatable team workflows, but buyers still struggle to compare product depth, evidence quality, and deployment fit.
research_question: Which AI coding product direction shows the strongest near-term opportunity for a practical market entry?
core_conclusion: A workflow-focused AI coding product aimed at small software teams has the clearest path, especially when it emphasizes trusted outputs, review support, and deployment readiness.

key_evidence.title: Adoption is becoming operational
key_evidence.body: Teams increasingly treat AI coding as part of delivery workflow rather than a novelty. Buyers want support for review, traceability, and rollout discipline.
key_evidence.source: Public product launches, engineering blogs, and workflow docs

key_evidence.title: Trust is the main purchase filter
key_evidence.body: Users will trial impressive generation, but longer-term usage depends on whether the system is explainable, reviewable, and easy to fit into an existing stack.

dimensions.title: Demand
dimensions.body: Interest is strong across founders, solo builders, and small engineering teams, with the highest pull around speed-up for existing workflows.

dimensions.title: Differentiation
dimensions.body: Pure generation is crowded. Workflow control, evidence-backed outputs, and decision support create a more defensible wedge.

dimensions.title: Go-to-market
dimensions.body: A self-serve entry with strong sample outputs and clear team value should reduce friction, but pricing needs to align with visible ROI.

charts.title: Relative signal strength by purchase factor
charts.note: Higher values indicate stronger recurring decision weight in the market scan.

uncertainty: Market narratives are moving fast, and some vendor claims are difficult to validate independently. Larger-team procurement behavior may differ from small-team behavior.
gaps: Need stronger bottom-up pricing sensitivity evidence
Need more direct buyer interviews from engineering managers
Need validation of long-term retention drivers beyond trial usage
risk_block: Competition is intense and feature parity can happen quickly if differentiation stays at the UI layer.
action_block: Validate one narrow workflow wedge with concrete example reports and team review loops before broadening the product surface.
recommendations: Build around a high-trust workflow: structured outputs, evidence tracking, clear artifacts, and handoff quality. Avoid leading with raw generation alone.

sources.name: Official product and docs review
sources.detail: Vendor documentation and launch material reviewed for workflow claims and deployment framing.

sources.name: Public market commentary
sources.detail: Industry analysis and engineering discussions used to compare positioning and trust concerns.

decision_panel: Proceed with a narrow workflow-focused product concept and use evidence-backed reports as the trust layer.
